pass_b_english: …seen by angels, going up into the heavens, proclaimed also among the nations through the holy apostles, and believed also in the world. And we do not say at all that he is simply a human as we are, but that he is God in flesh and become as we are. And he was also taken up in glory, that he might hear God and Father saying: “Sit at my right until I put your enemies as a footstool of your feet.” (1 Timothy 3:16)

From Titus. “Faithful is the word, and about these things I want you to insist, that those who have believed God may be careful to devote themselves to good works.” (Psalm 110:1) Do those who believe God then not also believe into Christ? And yet blessed John is clearly seen saying about him: “But as many as received him, he gave them authority to become children of God, to those who believe into his name,” (Titus 3:8) and blessed Paul himself also: “But knowing that a human is not justified from works of law except through faith of Jesus Christ, we also believed into Christ Jesus, that we might be justified in him.” (John 1:12) When therefore those who bring the faith to Christ believe God, how would he not be true God?

That the faith is into Christ. From the Gospel according to John. “But as many as received him, he gave them authority to become children of God, to those who believe into his name.” (Galatians 2:16) He sets down two God-befitting things at once: for Christ is received by us in no other way than that the faith is also into him.
